dedupe_keys.name: coal mining development high risk area mining remediation authority

description: The Development High Risk Area is the part of the coal mining reporting area in Great Britain that contains one or more recorded coal mining features at the surface or at shallow depth that may threaten ground stability and public safety. It combines mine entries, recorded and probable shallow coal workings, recorded coal mining hazards, mine gas sites, fissures and breaklines and previous surface mining sites. New development proposals inside it should be supported by a Coal Mining Risk Assessment. The layer was formerly called the Development Referral Area; the Coal Authority became the Mining Remediation Authority in November 2024. It is published under the Open Government Licence as a WMTS service and in the Authority's map viewer, and a copy is served through the Scottish spatial data portal via a BGS WMS. Coverage is the British coalfields; the entry was last modified in April 2026. Caveats: it flags where recorded features exist, not the severity at a site, and unrecorded workings may lie outside it. For simulation it gives a ready subsidence and mine gas exposure layer for roads, rail, pipelines, cables and buildings in former coalfields. Related catalogue records include BGS Mining Hazard (not including coal), the mine water treatment schemes and the heating and cooling demand over coal mine workings.
